claim: On any parent cycle path_up returns [] instead of stopping at the first repeated id, so a start id that names an entry yields no entry at all (path_up([a<a], "a") = [], and from the leaf of a writer-shaped journal whose header's parent_id is the leaf, also []).
witness: es=[{id:"a",parent_id:"a"}] start="a" -> [] (D4 rule 1 and the twin ev_path_up: [a]); es=[{id:"0000",parent_id:"0002"},{id:"0001",parent_id:"0000"},{id:"0002",parent_id:"0001"}] start="0002" -> [] (twin: [0000,0001,0002])
notes: Cause: journal.ail:1405 `else if contains_string(seen, id) then []` (should be `then acc`, as the comment and ADR-003 D4 rule 1 say). The twin ev_path_up (reader.ail:1226) has `then acc`, and its SOURCE pin sha256 db222e4c... is exactly the hash of the core body with `then acc` (negative_control.sh recomputes it), so this line changed after the twin was pinned; find_entry and contains_string still match their pins. Executed: path_props.ail exhaustive (ids {a,b,c}, parents {"",a,b,c,missing}, lists of length <= 4, 5 start ids): 44,970 of 271,205 cases violate P5.3, every one also a twin disagreement; run_random.sh seed 7, 2,100 cases up to 60 entries: 960, and seed 11, 4,200 cases: 1,921 (all from cycles, all twin disagreements). P5.1, P5.2 and P5.3's chain clause hold on every case. Under the pinned body (negative_control.sh M1) this repro, the whole-fold repro below (with fold_journal from the M1 copy) and all 18,080 length-3 cases pass. Whole-fold consequence on UNMODIFIED code (`bash ../out/repro/run.sh fold_cycle.ail` from the tree root, exit 1): a journal_lines_of_records journal with the header's parent_id set to the leaf is refused by fold_journal with `header` (a misleading refusal: the header is there), while the twin eval_fold_journal accepts it with the full history, so resume and the eval reader disagree. Reachability: the host writer never writes a cycle (parent_id = previous leaf; the one header rewrite keeps parent_id), so a hand-edited or corrupt journal, or a future branch/rewind operation (ADR-003 D8), is needed. It fails closed.

claim: When the start id is "" and an entry has id "", path_up returns [] because the root-sentinel test `if id == "" then acc` runs before the lookup, though the start id names an entry (the reader's strict_path returns that entry).
notes: Not the planted change: the twin ev_path_up has the same line and matches its pin, so this predates the snapshot. Executed: path_props.ail with ids {a,b,c,""}, length <= 3: 4,805 P5.3 violations, all with start "", and 1,273 cases where strict_path accepts a path while path_up returns []; random 'weird' generator: 40 of 70 (seed 7) and 65 of 121 (seed 11) start-"" cases. With M1 and the lookup forced (negative_control.sh M2) the repro exits 0. Reachability: journal_entry_of_json accepts "id": "" (at_string takes any string), and journal_leaf returns "" when the last line's id is "", so fold_journal then refuses with `header`; the host writer always writes zero-padded seq ids, so a hand-edited or foreign journal is needed. The sentinel collision also means an entry with id "" can never be reached as anyone's parent. Arguably a decoder-strictness gap (an empty id should be refused), but as registered P5.3 does not hold. Low severity.

claim: path_up's running time is quadratic in the path length (each step re-scans the entry list with find_entry and `seen` with contains_string): on a writer-shaped linear journal a 4x longer path costs 12-20x the time (2,000 entries: 16-39 s, 4,000: 62-124 s), and fold_journal on writer journals takes 0.85 s / 2.4 s / 8.2 s / 38 s at 254 / 504 / 1,004 / 2,004 lines.
witness: es = 0000<"", 0001<0000, ..., NNNN<NNNN-1 in file order, start = the leaf; n=400 vs n=1600
notes: Timing-based: perf_path.ail main times path_up in-process (std/clock) at n=400 and n=1600 and prints DEFECT PRESENT when the ratio exceeds 8 (linear ~4, quadratic ~16); measured ratios 12.5, 13.9 and 20.2 over three runs (20.2 at n=500/2000 is in runs/perf.txt; 13.9 is the repro command itself, 17 s; 12.5 was an earlier unlogged run). The machine was shared with other sessions (load ~15 on 8 cores), so absolute times vary about 2x between runs; the ratio is the claim. A linear-time walk (an id index built once) was not written, so the exit-0 side of this repro is untested. Not shown: that real journals reach this size; the repo's evidence journals have 10-23 lines. The fold's own comment treats quadratic cost as a defect ('`++ [m]` per entry would be quadratic in the thing the journal exists to make cheap'), and the fold runs on every --resume (rpc.ail:557). Separate from cost, P5.1 holds for long paths: the walk is constant-stack (depth_check.sh: 300 entries under --max-recursion-depth 20, while a non-tail control dies there).
